current_text.html: Amendments to the Book of Church Order may be made only in the following manner: 1. Approval of the proposed amendment by majority of those present and voting in the General Assembly, and its recommendation to the Presbyteries. 2. The advice and consent of two-thirds (2/3) of the Presbyteries. 3. The approval and enactment by a subsequent General Assembly by a majority of those present and voting.

recommendations.note: Recommendation and study papers are not comprehensively indexed by provision.

relationships.title: Grant Constitutional Status to BCO 53 re Preaching

metadata.summary: The CCB found no constitutional conflict in an overture to grant constitutional status to BCO 53 governing the ministry of preaching.

relationships.title: Preaching, or Teaching by Women in Worship

metadata.summary: The CCB found that amending BCO 53 to expressly disallow women from exhorting, preaching, or teaching in corporate worship is not in conflict with the BCO.

relationships.title: Amend BCO 17 by Adding a Clause Which Prohibits Ordination for Men Who Self-Identify as 'Gay Christians,' 'Same-sex Attracted Christians,' 'Homosexual Christians,' or Like Terms

metadata.summary: The CCB found this overture to amend BCO 17 prohibiting ordination of men using gay-identity labels to be in conflict with existing BCO provisions, though it was adopted.

relationships.title: Amend BCO 7 by Addition to Disqualify Same-sex Attracted Men from Ordination

metadata.summary: An overture from Westminster Presbytery to amend BCO 7 and related provisions disqualifying same-sex attracted men from ordination was found in conflict and adopted.

relationships.title: Altering and Refining the Language of BCO 59

metadata.summary: The CCB found Calvary Presbytery's overture to revise BCO 59 in conflict with the Constitution, as proposed changes to marriage publication and consent conflicted with BCO Preliminary Principle 7, BCO 11-2, BCO 29-1, and WCF 20.2.

A Grace Presbytery overture to amend and elevate BCO 59 was likewise in conflict, as granting full constitutional status constitutes adding to the BCO and requires the BCO amendment process per BCO 26-2.

relationships.title: The Roles and Description of Unordained Deaconesses and Deacon Assistants

metadata.summary: CCB found Grace Presbytery's overture on deaconesses and women officers in conflict with the Constitution, noting the session, not the congregation, is the appointing body requiring vows.

A Calvary Presbytery overture to elevate BCO 59 to full constitutional status was in conflict because doing so is equivalent to amending the BCO and requires the same multi-stage approval process under BCO 26-2.

relationships.title: Procedure for Dealing with Alleged Conflicts Between Scripture and the Constitution of the PCA

metadata.summary: The CCB found Eastern Canada Presbytery's overture in conflict with the Constitution because it would allow a General Assembly to bypass constitutional processes and permit modification of commission reports.

metadata.synopsis: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

metadata.synopsis: After a congregation voted to ask that all ruling elders' official relationships be dissolved without censure, the Session concurred and requested an interim Session. The SJC denied the elders' complaint, holding that BCO 24-6b extends by good and necessary deduction from one elder to multiple identified elders. Dissolution ended their service on that Session but did not divest them of office. Because both the congregation and Session requested it, BCO 13-9 and 15-2 authorized Presbytery to appoint an interim Session. A separate constitutional inquiry was denied without explanation.
